question: How many sector-allocation records have allocation_pct above 40, grouped by sector?
sql_query:
SELECT sector, COUNT(*) AS allocation_record_count
            FROM ATOM_ENTITY_SECTOR_ALLOCATION_001
            WHERE allocation_pct > 40
            GROUP BY sector;
sql_reason: COUNT(*) with WHERE allocation_pct>40 grouped by sector correctly answers the question.

question: How do average liquidity_score and average diversification_score compare across risk-score bands?
sql_query:
SELECT CASE
                       WHEN risk_score < 33 THEN 'risk_score < 33'
                       WHEN risk_score < 67 THEN 'risk_score 33-66'
                       ELSE 'risk_score >= 67'
                   END AS risk_score_band,
                   ROUND(AVG(liquidity_score), 2) AS avg_liquidity_score,
                   ROUND(AVG(diversification_score), 2) AS avg_diversification_score
            FROM ATOM_ENTITY_PORTFOLIO_HEALTH_001
            GROUP BY risk_score_band;
sql_reason: CASE-based banding with per-band AVG on a single table faithfully answers the question.

question: Which investors have liquidity_score below 20?
sql_query:
SELECT p.investor_id, p.investor_name, h.liquidity_score
            FROM ATOM_ENTITY_INVESTOR_PROFILE_001 p
            JOIN ATOM_ENTITY_PORTFOLIO_HEALTH_001 h ON h.investor_id = p.investor_id
            WHERE h.liquidity_score < 20;
sql_reason: 1:1 profile-health join with WHERE liquidity_score<20 faithfully answers the question with no fan-out risk.

question: Which investors have at least one holding with returns_pct below -20?
sql_query:
SELECT DISTINCT p.investor_id, p.investor_name
            FROM ATOM_ENTITY_INVESTOR_PROFILE_001 p
            JOIN ATOM_ENTITY_PORTFOLIO_HOLDING_001 o ON o.investor_id = p.investor_id
            WHERE o.returns_pct < -20;
sql_reason: DISTINCT investor_id over the holding join correctly returns investors with at least one holding below -20% return.

question: Which investors have at least one sector allocation with allocation_pct above 60?
sql_query:
SELECT DISTINCT p.investor_id, p.investor_name
            FROM ATOM_ENTITY_INVESTOR_PROFILE_001 p
            JOIN ATOM_ENTITY_SECTOR_ALLOCATION_001 a ON a.investor_id = p.investor_id
            WHERE a.allocation_pct > 60;
sql_reason: DISTINCT investor_id with allocation_pct>60 faithfully lists the concentrated investors.

question: For each profile risk_tolerance value, how many investors have risk_score above 70?
sql_query:
SELECT p.risk_tolerance,
                   COUNT(*) AS investor_count
            FROM ATOM_ENTITY_INVESTOR_PROFILE_001 p
            JOIN ATOM_ENTITY_PORTFOLIO_HEALTH_001 h ON h.investor_id = p.investor_id
            WHERE h.risk_score > 70
            GROUP BY p.risk_tolerance;
sql_reason: Health is one-per-investor so COUNT(*) equals distinct investors per risk_tolerance; no fan-out.

question: For each holding sector, how many holdings have returns_pct below 0?
sql_query:
SELECT o.sector, COUNT(*) AS negative_holding_count
            FROM ATOM_ENTITY_INVESTOR_PROFILE_001 p
            JOIN ATOM_ENTITY_PORTFOLIO_HOLDING_001 o ON o.investor_id = p.investor_id
            WHERE o.returns_pct < 0
            GROUP BY o.sector;
sql_reason: COUNT(*) of holding rows per sector correctly counts holdings as asked.

question: For each allocation sector, how many distinct investors have allocation_pct above 40?
sql_query:
SELECT a.sector,
                   COUNT(DISTINCT p.investor_id) AS investor_count
            FROM ATOM_ENTITY_INVESTOR_PROFILE_001 p
            JOIN ATOM_ENTITY_SECTOR_ALLOCATION_001 a ON a.investor_id = p.investor_id
